solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One curing heartbreak? Inspiring film song of the Fifties

indicators.note: inspiring literally means breathing in, so the first phrase takes the film's letters inside it

parts.note: someone who mends a broken heart could whimsically be called a love mender
E.T. is Spielberg's 1982 film about a stranded alien

explanation.surface: A question about a soothing hit song of the 1950s that eases a broken heart, from a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' looks part of the definition (the song was also a film title) but supplies the alien's letters; 'Inspiring' means taking them in.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvis Presley's 1956 ballad, also the title of his first film, is a famous Fifties song.

clue.text: Practical joke on jerk

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
to jerk something is to pull it sharply

explanation.surface: A prank played on some unfortunate jerk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' looks like a link word but is the cricket term: the on side of the field is the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoax that fools someone, making them believe a tall tale, is a playful trick of this name.

clue.text: Maybe I am behind first of lapwings, flock of geese going overhead?

indicators.note: in a down entry, the formation's letter sits above the rest

parts.note: migrating geese fly in a V-shaped formation
to be behind with payments is to owe money

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of lapwings

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher trails some lapwings while a skein of geese flies overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe I' is the definition: the letter I is one example of the category.
explanation.definitionFit: The letter I is one of the five letters A, E, I, O, U that represent open speech sounds.

clue.text: Man secreting a note, as source for copper

indicators.note: secreting means hiding away, so the word for man holds the next pieces

parts.note: a man is a male
a chit is a short written note

explanation.surface: A man hides a note, perhaps a tip-off for the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a police officer, but here it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: This green mineral is a carbonate ore from which the metal copper is extracted.

clue.text: Orderly's contract

definitions.meaning: neat and tidy, in good order
to cut down or reduce in size

explanation.surface: A hospital orderly's employment contract.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both neat in appearance and to cut back or reduce, as in shrinking a budget.

clue.text: Who's on an unmanned spacecraft keeping dry part of the rocket?

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the crew phrase holds the word for dry

parts.note: an unmanned craft carries nobody, no one
sec is the wine term for dry

explanation.surface: A question about who rides an unmanned craft while keeping part of the rocket dry.
explanation.walkthrough: The question 'Who's on an unmanned spacecraft?' is answered, not defined: nobody is aboard. 'Keeping' means that answer holds the wine word for dry.
explanation.definitionFit: The pointed front section of a rocket or missile carries this name.

clue.text: Thirsty, English drink uncorked?

indicators.note: uncorked takes off the top of the drink, its first letter

parts.note: lager is a drink

explanation.surface: A thirsty Englishman wants his drink opened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncorked' removes the L from LAGER, leaving AGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirsty can mean keenly wanting something, as in thirsty for knowledge, so it is a synonym of keen.

clue.text: Show characters around Asian island, as mystic

indicators.note: around means the cast surrounds the island

parts.note: the characters of a show are its cast
Bali is an island of Indonesia

explanation.surface: A theatre company tours an Asian island, playing a mystic.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the Kabbalah, Jewish esoteric teaching, is a type of mystic.

clue.text: Long-distance runner cut over peak in Nepal

indicators.note: in a down entry, over puts the word for cut above the letter

parts.note: to sever is to cut

indicators.note: peak in takes the top letter of Nepal

explanation.surface: A marathon runner is injured on a Himalayan peak in Nepal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' is a river: the Severn is Britain's longest river.
explanation.definitionFit: A river runs, and this is the longest river in Britain, flowing through Wales and England.

clue.text: Disappear, somehow like gas masks on worried faces

indicators.note: masks means covers up, so the rearranged letters hold the next ones
somehow says the letters of like gas are rearranged
faces takes the front letters of on and worried

explanation.surface: Worried people put on gas masks, perhaps in a wartime drill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' turns LIKE GAS into GALKIES; 'masks' puts OW inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British idiom for going missing, from taking a dog for a walk.

clue.text: Serious mark of a French writer?

definitions.meaning: an accent written in French, as in the è of père

explanation.surface: A question about a serious French author's distinguishing trait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' is not a grade or a trait but an accent sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Solemn means the same; the backward-sloping accent is common in French writing.

clue.text: Free country holding Nationalist officer back

indicators.note: holding means the country contains the other pieces

parts.note: UK is the United Kingdom

indicators.note: back says the officer's letters are read in reverse

parts.note: Col is the abbreviation for colonel

explanation.surface: A country detains a nationalist officer and is told to release him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' is a verb here, not an adjective; 'back' turns the colonel's abbreviation round before 'holding' places it in the country.
explanation.definitionFit: To open a lock releases what was secured, so the verb is a synonym of release.

clue.text: Gangster, warmer one

parts.note: a scarf warms the neck
an ace counts as one in cards

explanation.surface: A gangster is a nicer fellow than another one.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname of Al Capone and the title of gangster films with Paul Muni and Al Pacino.

clue.text: Roman once dropping in by way of the country

indicators.note: dropping means letting go of the word in

parts.note: Latin was the language of ancient Romans
via means by way of

explanation.surface: An ancient Roman drops in on his way through the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping in' looks like visiting, but it removes IN from LATIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A Baltic state lying between Estonia and Lithuania.

clue.text: Rejected role, cross, having to go up a hole leading to the stage

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the role is read in reverse

parts.note: a part is a role in a play

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up reads the cross from the bottom

parts.note: a rood is a crucifix

explanation.surface: An actor angry at being turned down for a part.
explanation.walkthrough: A rood is a cross, especially one above a church screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged opening in the stage floor through which actors can rise or vanish.

clue.text: Sloth, one I cannot fancy

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone admits they cannot fancy a lazy partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' turns I CANNOT into NACTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloth, one of the deadly sins, is laziness: a refusal to do anything.

clue.text: Wingers for Chelsea ineffectual, lacking goals

indicators.note: wingers play on the edges, so this takes the outer letters of Chelsea

parts.note: useless means ineffectual

explanation.surface: Chelsea's wide players are ineffectual and can't score. Chelsea is a London football club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goals' is not football scoring but aims or purposes.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no reason or purpose behind it, an action with no motive.

clue.text: Kill fish then tailless rat

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish

indicators.note: tailless means losing the final letter

parts.note: a rotter is a rat, a contemptible person

explanation.surface: A recipe for killing a fish and then a rat with no tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailless' drops the final R of ROTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To strangle someone with a cord or wire, an old method of execution.

clue.text: Getting kiss finally, quickie, one's off on a long journey

definitions.text: one's off on a long journey

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of kiss

parts.note: in cricket a pace man is a fast bowler

explanation.surface: A quick kiss before someone sets off on a long trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quickie' is a fast bowler in cricket, a paceman.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronaut travels far through the cosmos, a long journey indeed.

clue.text: Well-groomed tree

explanation.definitionFit: The word means neat and smartly dressed, and also names a common conifer.

clue.text: In US, a Texas capital, possibly?

definitions.text: In US, a Texas capital, possibly?

indicators.note: possibly says the letters may be arranged another way
capital takes the first letter of Texas

explanation.surface: A question about a state capital in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' shuffles IN US A with T. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The state capital of Texas is this city.

clue.text: Doffing cap, gallant on frequent occasions

indicators.note: doffing a cap removes the head, so the first letter goes

parts.note: knightly means chivalrous, gallant

explanation.surface: A gallant man tips his hat often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doffing cap' drops the K of KNIGHTLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Happening every evening, so very frequently.

clue.text: Seen before dawn, very rare bird

indicators.note: seen before puts the colour ahead of the beginning

parts.note: very rare meat is still red
the dawn of something is its start

explanation.surface: A rare bird spotted before daybreak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very rare' is not scarcity but meat barely cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: A small songbird with a red tail, a member of the thrush family.

clue.text: A fly going up bikini

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up reads the letters from the bottom

parts.note: a gnat is a small fly

explanation.surface: A fly crawls up someone's swimsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going up' reverses A GNAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny swimsuit or briefs with narrow strings at the sides, a style of two-piece.

clue.text: Survive hunger, as fit

parts.note: to be is to exist or live on
to long is to hunger for something

explanation.surface: Someone survives hunger and stays healthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' looks like healthy but is the verb: to fit in.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that fit in their proper place are where they should be.

clue.text: Elder beyond old, as native American

indicators.note: beyond places the elder after the old

parts.note: a sage is a wise elder

explanation.surface: A tribal elder past old age.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sioux-speaking people of the Great Plains, now in Oklahoma.

clue.text: Possibly sleeping in solitude, baby turning over

indicators.note: turning over says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A baby in quiet solitude turns over in the cot.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in bed may mean being asleep, though not always, hence possibly.

clue.text: Card player put in virtually double for joker

indicators.note: put in means the player is placed inside
virtually means nearly all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a clone is an exact double
in bridge the four players are North, South, East and West

explanation.surface: A card player is brought in as almost a double for the joker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Virtually' trims CLONE to CLON; 'put in' adds W inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus performer who jokes and fools around for laughs.

clue.text: Contents of cellar Neuburger and Claret — luckily all for opening?

parts.words: Neuburger and Claret — luckily all for opening
parts.note: the opening letters of Neuburger, and, Claret, luckily spell the chemical formula NaCl

explanation.surface: A wine cellar holds Neuburger and claret, ready for opening.
explanation.walkthrough: NaCl, sodium chloride, is the chemical name for the answer. 'Cellar' is a salt cellar, not a wine store.
explanation.definitionFit: A salt cellar is the shaker or dish on a dining table holding salt.

clue.text: I'm astonished! A shed converted into fruit shop!

parts.note: ha! is a cry of surprise

indicators.note: into puts the converted letters inside the fruit

parts.note: a berry is a fruit

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form

explanation.surface: Surprise that a garden shed has become a greengrocer's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Converted' turns A SHED into DASHE, which goes into BER-RY.
explanation.definitionFit: A store selling sewing goods such as buttons, ribbons and thread.
